target_customer: Freelancers, contractors and other workers without employer benefits
problem: Independent workers had to assemble tax withholding, time off savings, retirement and health insurance themselves.
business_model: Consumer fintech and insurance brokerage (commissions, personal payroll); later broker-only model under new owners

founders.name: Kristen Anderson
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in the 2021 Series A press release; not listed on the YC page.

exit.reason: Founders shut the company down in March 2023; the new owners bought it and relaunched in October 2023.

competitors.name: Freelancers Union
competitors.what: Health insurance and benefits access for independent workers
competitors.traction_then: Over 500,000 members per a later source summary

technical_complexity.rationale: Bank-connected income detection, automated withholding and insurance enrollment need integrations and compliance but are standard fintech engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Insurance brokering and withholding were replicable; no sourced network or data moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed it; the company shut in March 2023 and was sold to individuals.

market_need_then: Gig and freelance work was growing in 2019 and policy debate on portable benefits (BenefitsPro 2019, AB5 in California) highlighted the gap.

branding.domain_note: Used catch.co rather than catch.com; the same name is used by many unrelated companies.

identity.logo: New symbol and colors introduced in March 2022 rebrand

rebrands.why: Company said it reflected the evolution of Catch and of work itself

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly short name but generic and shared across many companies; a 2022 rebrand is documented but no evidence of community or viral pull.

outcome_analysis: Catch raised a seed in 2019 and a 12 million dollar Series A in July 2021, then shut down in March 2023 and was sold the same month to two individuals who relaunched it as a free insurance broker in October 2023. The cause of the shutdown is not public in the sources found, so no failure factors are assigned. YC lists it as Acquired, which matches the sale to its new owners rather than a corporate acquirer.
notes: Seed size conflicts: TechCrunch (via search summary) 5.1 million at 20.5 million post-money after a 1 million pre-seed; the 2021 press release and FinSMEs say 8 million seed in 2019. Press release opened; TechCrunch figures seen only in a search summary. One summary cites total 18.1 million raised; others sum to 20 million. Pre-seed not recorded as a round. Shutdown cause not public.
